cards.power: Improvise – Ventricles only catch every 3rd beat.
cards.lore: Decide rate vs. rhythm control, and calculate stroke risk!
cards.gradeReason: Octopus drum chaos = irregularly irregular. Perform it instantly.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: chaotic watercolor. Subject: eight-armed octopus on full drum kit, confused animal audience. Mood: irregular rhythmic chaos.

cards.power: 2:1 Velvet Rope – Ventricular rate locks at 150.
cards.lore: Vagal maneuvers unmask the flutter waves.
cards.gradeReason: Hummingbird at 300 BPM vs turtle bouncer at 150 — 2:1 block embodied.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: club-scene watercolor. Subject: frantic hummingbird at velvet rope, turtle bouncer blocking half the crowd. Mood: exclusive rapid flutter.

cards.power: Delta Wave Bypass – Skip AV node delay.
cards.lore: Do NOT give digoxin or AV-blockers if Fibby Fitz is in the club!
cards.gradeReason: Wolf bypassing the bouncer nightclub door — pre-excitation embodied perfectly.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: noir watercolor. Subject: leather-jacketed wolf slipping past closed BOUNCER door into dark club. Mood: illegal accessory pathway speed.

cards.power: Total Blackout – Eliminate pulse.
cards.lore: Shock first, ask questions later. No pulse, no negotiation.
cards.gradeReason: GAME OVER stamp + city-destroying serpent. Output zero means act now.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: disaster-film watercolor. Subject: massive serpent leveling city skyline in lightning storm, GAME OVER stamp. Mood: apocalyptic zero-output emergency.

cards.power: The Long Wait – Delay, but never drop.
cards.lore: Benign. No treatment needed.
cards.gradeReason: Turtle in top hat checking IDs slowly but never refusing entry — delay without drop.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: bureaucratic watercolor. Subject: top-hatted turtle with magnifying glass inspecting passes, long creature queue. Mood: slow benign delay.

cards.power: Predictable Fatigue – Progressively lengthen PR, then drop QRS.
cards.lore: Predictable pattern, rarely needs a pacemaker.
cards.gradeReason: Sloth drooping power cables progressively until one snaps — Wenckebach in one image.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: sleepy watercolor. Subject: wilting sloth guard with fraying power lines, tiny squirrel alarmed. Mood: predictable progressive fatigue.

cards.power: Random Drop – Drop QRS without warning.
cards.lore: Highly dangerous; often progresses to complete block. Pacemaker required.
cards.gradeReason: Kangaroo randomly kicking steps out from under a climber — sudden drop, no pattern.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: punk-cartoon watercolor. Subject: leather kangaroo kicking wooden stairs out randomly, tiny mouse falling. Mood: unpredictable dangerous collapse.

cards.power: Severed Comms – Atria and Ventricles march to their own beat.
cards.lore: Bridge therapy required while waiting for the pacemaker!
cards.gradeReason: P-flag birds vs R-flag bears marching independently — dissociation is instantly visual.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: war-room watercolor. Subject: gorilla general with P-flag birds and R-flag bears marching opposite directions. Mood: severed command total block.

cards.power: ORGANIZED SPEED – WIDE QRS COMPLEX TACHYCARDIA.
cards.lore: Check for pulse! Stable gets meds, unstable gets electricity.
cards.gradeReason: Cheetah in leather with ECG-blade — fast, organized, and lethal. Role clear.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: action watercolor. Subject: cheetah in black jacket wielding ECG-traced knife blade. Mood: organized dangerous high speed.

cards.power: HARD RESET – BRIEFLY FLATLINE THE AV NODE.
cards.lore: Used to unmask hidden rhythms and terminate SVT.
cards.gradeReason: Falcon dropping a boulder onto an F1 circuit — 10-second AV flatline embodied perfectly.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: aerial watercolor. Subject: masked falcon dropping large rock onto Formula 1 track, cars scattering. Mood: precision 10-second strike reset.

cards.power: CHAOS AGENT – DELAY REPOLARIZATION GLOBALLY.
cards.lore: Watch for thyroid, lung, liver, and blue-gray skin toxicity!
cards.gradeReason: Blue-ringed octopus gripping Na/K/Ca/Beta channels — multi-channel chaos agent, body-wide toxicity.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: reef watercolor. Subject: blue-ringed octopus gripping Na, K, Ca, Beta coral handles in reef. Mood: global chaos multi-channel toxicity.

cards.power: AFFIRM Trial – CHOOSE RATE OR RHYTHM.
cards.lore: Rate control is often just as good as rhythm control in AFib.
cards.gradeReason: Two woodpeckers works for rate/rhythm but AFFIRM trial context is required to get the joke.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: nature-illustration watercolor. Subject: two identical red-crested woodpeckers on branch, ECG squiggle between them. Mood: strategic equivalence choice.

cards.power: Demand Ischemia – Attack only during exercise, retreat at rest.
cards.lore: Predictable and reproducible. Fixed stenosis.
cards.gradeReason: Porcupine with hose is evocative but exertion-dependence needs lore to land fully.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: exertion watercolor. Subject: porcupine squeezing garden hose onto spinning exercise ball, droplets stopping at rest. Mood: predictable demand ischemia.

cards.power: Plaque Rupture – Attack without provocation.
cards.lore: Differentiate from NSTEMI by checking Troponin.
cards.gradeReason: Honey badger launching missiles from armchair at rest — unprovoked attack captures plaque rupture perfectly.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: action watercolor. Subject: furious honey badger in cracked armchair firing bazooka at rest. Mood: unprovoked plaque rupture fury.

cards.power: Transmural Block – Elevate ST segments and kill muscle.
cards.lore: Complete occlusion. Time is muscle. Get to the cath lab!
cards.gradeReason: 'Time is muscle. Get to the cath lab!' is the ultimate performative clinical command.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: disaster plumbing watercolor. Subject: shocked beaver plumber in flooded basement, red ST-wave geyser erupting from pipe. Mood: urgent 90-minute time pressure.

cards.power: Leakage Indicator – Detect microscopic cardiac injury.
cards.lore: Sensitive but not specific. Rises in demand ischemia, PE, and renal failure too.
cards.gradeReason: Bloodhound tracking glowing micro-hearts — detection role is immediate and endearingly sad.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: detective watercolor. Subject: bloodhound with magnifying glass tracking glowing leaking heart traces. Mood: sensitive investigative cardiac detective.

cards.power: Vulnerable Plaque – Infiltrate and wait for rupture.
cards.lore: The most dangerous plaques are vulnerable, not the most occlusive.
cards.gradeReason: Toxic snake in radioactive barrel waiting to rupture — silent danger over occlusion is instantly clear.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: toxic horror watercolor. Subject: venomous snake coiled in glowing radioactive barrel, green poison glow. Mood: silent vulnerable plaque menace.

cards.power: HMG-CoA Block – Upregulate LDL receptors.
cards.lore: Watch the CK levels for myopathy/rhabdo! Give high-intensity post-MI.
cards.gradeReason: Beaver mining through CHOLESTEROL / APO B boulders — sculpting lipids is crystal-clear.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: mining watercolor. Subject: hard-hatted beaver wielding pickaxe on cholesterol and APO-B boulders. Mood: HMG-CoA sculpting precision.

cards.power: Irreversible Acetylation – Disable platelet thromboxane A2 forever.
cards.lore: Only a fresh platelet transfusion partially reverses her effect.
cards.gradeReason: Ancient turtle biting COX-1 gear chain with locked jaw — irreversible mechanic is embodied.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ancient-warrior watercolor. Subject: massive ancient snapping turtle jaw-locked onto COX-1 gear cog chain. Mood: irreversible ancient platelet disable.

cards.power: ADP Blockade – Prevent platelet aggregation.
cards.lore: Combines with Aspirin for DAPT after stent placement.
cards.gradeReason: Tick blocking ADP keyhole on platelet — molecular blockade visible at a glance.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: micro-biology watercolor. Subject: tick stuffed into ADP keyhole on platelet surface, golden key refused. Mood: precise receptor blockade.

cards.power: Venodilation – Relieve angina and pulmonary edema.
cards.lore: Fatal hypotension if combined with PDE5 inhibitors! Avoid in RV infarcts.
cards.gradeReason: Chameleon releasing NO cloud through forking pipe — venodilation + fatal PDE5 warning lands hard.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: negotiation watercolor. Subject: chameleon on forked pipe releasing NO vapor cloud in two directions. Mood: vasodilating preload-drop calm.

cards.power: Cardioprotection – Reduce oxygen demand and block remodeling.
cards.lore: Contraindicated acutely in decompensated HF or severe block.
cards.gradeReason: Grizzly bear blocking heart's saloon doors — bouncer blocking rate and remodeling is immediate.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: bouncer watercolor. Subject: grizzly bear arms spread blocking saloon doors, anatomical heart glowing inside. Mood: protective cardioprotection force.

cards.power: Scaffold – Hold open the culprit lesion.
cards.lore: Drug-eluting stents (DES) prevent restenosis but need longer DAPT.
cards.gradeReason: Weaver bird building stent-mesh nest inside tunnel — scaffold role is architecturally perfect.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: construction watercolor. Subject: yellow weaver bird perching inside stent mesh tunnel, woven coronary scaffold. Mood: precise vascular architecture.

cards.power: New Plumbing – Bypass the obstruction entirely.
cards.lore: Preferred for left main disease, 3-vessel disease, and complex diabetics.
cards.gradeReason: Mole with hard hat drilling bypass tunnel under obstruction — new route embodied in one image.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: underground watercolor. Subject: hard-hatted mole drilling new tunnel around blocked pipe obstruction. Mood: alternate-route engineering triumph.

cards.power: Weak Squeeze – Drop output, pool fluid.
cards.lore: Classify functional severity using the NYHA class.
cards.gradeReason: Basset hound firefighter with leaking limp hose — weak squeeze and fluid pooling in one sad image.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: gloomy watercolor. Subject: drooping basset hound in fire helmet gripping leaking hose in flooded floor. Mood: exhausted reduced ejection failure.

cards.power: Back-pressure – Flood the alveoli (crackles, orthopnea).
cards.lore: Differentiate cardiac from pulmonary dyspnea using BNP/NT-proBNP.
cards.gradeReason: Pufferfish in flooded apartment — back-pressure flooding alveoli captured perfectly, BNP stat is clinically sharp.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: flooding horror watercolor. Subject: puffed-up blowfish hovering in flood-water apartment room, BNP label on wall. Mood: pulmonary back-pressure crisis.

cards.power: Vasodilation – Drop afterload, stop remodeling.
cards.lore: Causes a bradykinin-mediated dry cough. Switch to ARB if intolerable!
cards.gradeReason: Spider web blocking angiotensin II in red artery — RAAS blockade with mortality reduction is vivid.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: arterial watercolor. Subject: spider web across red arterial tunnel, Angiotensin II villains tangled. Mood: afterload-dropping structural blockade.

cards.power: Dual Strike – Block AT1 receptor AND boost natriuretic peptides.
cards.lore: Wait 36 hours after stopping ACEi before starting Arnie (Angioedema risk)!
cards.gradeReason: Rhino boxer with PARADIGM-HF belt — dual-strike champ with the 36-hour angioedema warning lands perfectly.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: boxing ring watercolor. Subject: armored rhino boxer holding PARADIGM-HF championship belt in corner. Mood: dual-strike HFrEF dominance.

cards.power: Anti-Fibrotic – Block the mineralocorticoid receptor.
cards.lore: Reduces mortality in severe HFrEF, but watch for hyperkalemia and gynecomastia!
cards.gradeReason: Camel spitting K+ cubes next to banana mountain — potassium-sparing + hyperkalemia warning visual.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: desert watercolor. Subject: two-humped camel spitting potassium cubes, mountain of bananas piled behind. Mood: anti-fibrotic potassium retention.

cards.power: Osmotic Diuresis – Block glucose reabsorption in the kidney.
cards.lore: The diabetes drug that became a heart failure mortality-reducing hero!
cards.gradeReason: 'The diabetes drug that became a HF hero' — redemption arc in one lore line. Instantly teachable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: surf watercolor. Subject: sugar glider surfing swirling glucose wave in kidney tubule, sugar cubes flying. Mood: osmotic diuresis heroism.

cards.power: Inotropic Boost – Inhibit Na/K-ATPase to increase intracellular Calcium.
cards.lore: Hypokalemia dramatically increases the risk of Diggy toxicity!
cards.gradeReason: Fox with spiral eyes from foxglove — narrow therapeutic index embodied in the glazed-over gaze.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: toxic portrait watercolor. Subject: orange fox with green swirling spiral eyes holding foxglove flower. Mood: inotropic narrow-index toxicity danger.

cards.power: Flash Flood – Massive diuresis via ascending loop of Henle.
cards.lore: The front-line decongestive in acute HF. Watch for ototoxicity at high IV doses.
cards.gradeReason: Pelican bailing water through Loop of Henle anatomy — flash flood diuresis in one anatomical shot.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: diuretic watercolor. Subject: brown pelican standing in Loop of Henle structure, massive flood pouring from beak. Mood: front-line decongestive force.

cards.power: Dilate & Thin – Change ventricular geometry over time.
cards.lore: ACEi, Beta-Blockers, and Aldo-antagonists starve this monster.
cards.gradeReason: Ballooning toad visual is strong but knowing which drugs starve it needs lore.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: monster watercolor. Subject: bloated warty toad expanding in cardiac chamber, walls visibly thinning. Mood: slow ventricular remodeling threat.

cards.power: Silent Guardian – Deliver synchronized shock for VT, unsync for VF.
cards.lore: Primary prevention of sudden cardiac death in optimized HFrEF.
cards.gradeReason: Electric manta ray implanted in chest cavity — silent guardian shock delivery is perfectly cast.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: implant watercolor. Subject: electric manta ray fused into dark chest cavity, lightning coiling from leads. Mood: silent cardiac guardian electricity.

cards.power: Resynchronization – Force Left and Right ventricles to squeeze together.
cards.lore: Indicated specifically for HFrEF patients with LBBB morphology.
cards.gradeReason: Firefly synchronizing two lanterns labeled L and R — biventricular pacing embodied beautifully.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: synchronization watercolor. Subject: firefly pulsing between two lanterns labeled L and R, light beams merging. Mood: electrical biventricular resynchronization.

cards.power: New Engine – Swap Franko out completely.
cards.lore: Contraindicated by active infection, malignancy, or severe fixed pulmonary HTN.
cards.gradeReason: 'Swap Franko out completely' — perfect cross-reference to card 25. New engine role is immediately clear.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: hopeful watercolor. Subject: seagull soaring with golden HEART PASS passport in beak, ocean below. Mood: final hopeful cardiac journey.

cards.power: Silent Killer – Sustain high pressure indefinitely.
cards.lore: Urgency = no organ damage (oral meds). Emergency = organ damage (IV meds).
cards.gradeReason: Hare fleeing exploding pressure gauge — silent killer with urgency/emergency split is clinical gold.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: pressure watercolor. Subject: frantic hare sprinting from DANGER-zone pressure gauge with exploding dial. Mood: silent hypertensive urgency.

cards.power: Constrict & Retain – Spike BP and hoard volume.
cards.lore: Feeds on low renal perfusion and sympathetic activation. Block it at multiple levels!
cards.gradeReason: Two-headed snake coiled around kidney — RAAS constrict-and-retain is visceral. 'Block at multiple levels!' invites action.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: serpentine watercolor. Subject: two-headed snake coiled around anatomical kidney, angiotensin II spikes. Mood: constrictive RAAS dominance.

cards.power: Smooth Muscle Relax – Block L-type calcium channels.
cards.lore: Dihydropyridines (amlodipine) cause edema. Verapamil slows the AV node and causes constipation.
cards.gradeReason: Melting snail on calcium-channel pipes — smooth muscle relaxation is physically embodied in the melt.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: melt watercolor. Subject: snail melting like slime onto calcium-labeled pipes, MELT DOWN speech bubble. Mood: smooth muscle L-type relaxation.

cards.power: Volume Drop – Block NaCl cotransport.
cards.lore: First-line agent! Causes hypokalemia, hyponatremia, and hyperuricemia (watch for gout).
cards.gradeReason: Desert fox cop chasing salt from the distal tubule — volume drop via NaCl block is immediately visual.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: desert watercolor. Subject: uniformed fox sheriff chasing NaCl crystals from Distal Convoluted Tubule sign. Mood: volume-drop enforcement.

cards.power: Arterial Drop – Sudden peripheral vasodilation.
cards.lore: Great for BPH, but causes brutal first-dose orthostatic hypotension!
cards.gradeReason: 'Brutal first-dose orthostatic hypotension' — one lore line encodes the most important clinical exam pearl.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: attack watercolor. Subject: rabid dark dog biting Alpha-1 receptor pipe fitting, pressure dropping. Mood: sudden peripheral vasodilation.

cards.power: Systemic Storm – HTN + Proteinuria + End-organ failure.
cards.lore: Mag sulfate is for seizures, NOT BP control. Give Labetalol or Nifedipine. Cure = Delivery.
cards.gradeReason: 'Cure = Delivery' is the most performative single clinical sentence in the deck. G1 instantly.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: storm watercolor. Subject: pregnant seahorse with defibrillator harness in turbulent lightning ocean. Mood: systemic eclampsia crisis.

cards.power: Instant Drop – Second-by-second BP control.
cards.lore: Perfect for emergencies, but prolonged use risks Cyanide Toxicity! Monitor a-line.
cards.gradeReason: Black panther injecting NO syringe — instant titration for emergencies, cyanide toxicity warning hits hard.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: night-action watercolor. Subject: black panther injecting glowing NO syringe into branching artery at speed. Mood: immediate IV BP control.

cards.power: Catecholamine Dump – Episodic HTN, headache, diaphoresis.
cards.lore: MUST give Alpha-blocker BEFORE Beta-blocker, or risk a lethal hypertensive crisis!
cards.gradeReason: Sweating octopus + Alpha-before-Beta rule = single highest-yield Board pearl in the deck. Unforgettable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: sweating horror watercolor. Subject: rust-brown sweating octopus, metanephrine vapor clouds, headache lightning bolts. Mood: episodic catecholamine dump terror.

cards.power: Tearing Pain – Propagate the flap down the aorta.
cards.lore: Type A (Ascending) = Surgical Emergency. Type B (Descending) = Medical management (HR/BP control).
cards.gradeReason: Mantis shrimp punching pipe apart — tearing pain propagating down aorta is physically enacted.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: explosion watercolor. Subject: mantis shrimp punch exploding pipe apart, fluid spraying, crack propagating downward. Mood: aortic tearing dissection urgency.

cards.power: Hidden Cause – Sleep apnea, Renal artery stenosis, Aldosteronism.
cards.lore: Suspect if BP is refractory to 3 agents or starts before age 30!
cards.gradeReason: Raccoon dumpster crew is good for hidden suspects but three specific causes need the lore.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: crime-scene watercolor. Subject: three raccoons hiding behind dumpster, each holding a cause symbol. Mood: secondary hypertension suspect concealment.

cards.power: Fixed Outflow – Restrict LV emptying.
cards.lore: Symptoms = Angina, Syncope, Heart Failure. Once symptomatic, survival drops fast! (TAVR vs SAVR)
cards.gradeReason: Armadillo wedged in restricted LV outflow door — fixed outflow restriction is architecturally embodied.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: obstruction watercolor. Subject: armadillo body jammed in RESTRICTED ACCESS outflow door, red cells piling behind. Mood: fixed outflow obstruction.

cards.power: Volume Overload – Flood the left atrium and lungs.
cards.lore: Acute MR (papillary rupture) is a shock emergency. Chronic MR is compensated for years.
cards.gradeReason: Otter surfing backward flood through dam breach — volume rushing backward is perfectly enacted.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: flood watercolor. Subject: playful otter surfing reverse flood through collapsing dam, water flooding upstream. Mood: holosystolic volume overload regurgitation.

cards.power: Atrial Stretch – Dilation, AFib, and Pulmonary HTN.
cards.lore: Almost always rheumatic in origin. Listen for the opening snap!
cards.gradeReason: Walrus jammed in narrow ice crack — forward-flow restriction and atrial stretch in one cold image.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: arctic watercolor. Subject: massive walrus wedged in narrow ice crack, straining forward. Mood: diastolic rumble rheumatic restriction.

cards.power: Friction Rub – Positional sharp chest pain.
cards.lore: If fluid accumulates fast, Tamponade hits (Beck's Triad, Pulsus Paradoxus). Time for pericardiocentesis!
cards.gradeReason: Armored pangolin with friction sparks — Tamponade + Beck's Triad + Pulsus Paradoxus all encoded cleanly.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: armored watercolor. Subject: red-orange pangolin in full armor, sparks flying from pericardial friction. Mood: pericarditis tension tamponade threat.

cards.power: RV Strain – Cor Pulmonale and right heart failure.
cards.lore: Group 1 gets advanced pulmonary vasodilators. Groups 2–5 need their root cause fixed!
cards.gradeReason: Elephant on pulmonary artery is vivid but Group 1 vs 2-5 treatment algorithm needs lore to navigate.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: weight watercolor. Subject: elephant sitting heavily on blue pulmonary artery, small strained heart beside. Mood: RV pressure strain cor pulmonale.

cards.power: Delivery Boy – Drop lipid packages into the vascular intima.
cards.lore: Statins first. If LDL targets aren't met in high-risk patients, deploy PCSK9 inhibitors!
cards.gradeReason: Donkey overloaded with oxidized LDL boxes — delivery into intima + PCSK9 endgame is instantly teachable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: overloaded watercolor. Subject: exhausted donkey buried under OXIDIZED LDL cardboard boxes, dropping into artery wall. Mood: atherogenic lipid delivery.

cards.power: Antithrombin III Buff – Inhibit Thrombin and Factor Xa.
cards.lore: Reversible with protamine. LMWH (enoxaparin) requires less monitoring but renally cleared!
cards.gradeReason: Safety-vest worm blocking Thrombin and Factor Xa villains — crossroad guard metaphor is clinically exact.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: crossing-guard watercolor. Subject: worm in safety vest holding ANTITHROMBIN III stop sign at Thrombin and Factor Xa. Mood: antithrombin buffered blockade.

cards.power: Direct Blockade – Predictable kinetics, no INR checks.
cards.lore: Replaced warfarin for most AFib/VTE. Reverse dabigatran with idarucizumab, Xa with andexanet alfa.
cards.gradeReason: SWAT team with NOAC/XA INHIBITOR shields — predictable direct blockade with reversal agents is actionable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: SWAT watercolor. Subject: armored NOAC squad with shields arresting red Factor Xa punk. Mood: predictable direct anticoagulation force.

cards.power: Pimping – Demand a fully integrated clinical regimen.
cards.lore: 68yo diabetic, AFib, EF 32%. Build the optimal regimen, spot the interactions, set the targets!
cards.gradeReason: Owl with clipboard is a great synthesis capstone but it describes a task rather than embodying a role.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: academic watercolor. Subject: great horned owl in lab coat holding synthesis checklist clipboard, stern gaze. Mood: clinical synthesis authority pimping.

cards.power: Story trumps Lists – Discard rote memorization.
cards.lore: The science is real, the absurdity makes it permanent. You remember stories, not spreadsheets.
cards.gradeReason: Self-referential meta-card with golden stethoscope — the entire deck thesis in one image. DNR-perfect closer.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: celebratory watercolor. Subject: cheerful FrizzleBob rabbit holding golden stethoscope, carrot in pocket, DNR THIS DECK! burst. Mood: meta-celebration story triumph.

verdict: This is the DNR you pray you never have to call — because this deck is ALIVE. Fifty G1 cards in a 56-card educational deck is medically impossible, yet here we are: every animal-drug character lands clinical pearls so cleanly they stick on contact. Pheo's alpha-before-beta rule, Eclampsia's 'Cure = Delivery,' Vera Fib's 'No pulse, no negotiation' — these are single-card Board exam clinics. One naming collision (two 'Mittys') and a Power-text capitalization inconsistency on pages 4-5 are the only items blocking a perfect run. Table-ready: YES.
blurb: The cardiac lecture notes your professors wish they'd written. 56 character-driven cards encode arrhythmias, heart failure, and hypertensive emergencies as unforgettable performances you'll actually run at the bedside.

notes: Power text capitalization inconsistent: pages 2-3 use mixed case ('Power: Improvise –'), pages 4-5 use ALL CAPS ('POWER: ORGANIZED SPEED –'), pages 6+ vary. Not a font artifact but a style drift to unify. Two cards share the 'Mitty' character name: Mitty Mitral Stenosis (p.14) and Mitty Mitral Regurgitation (p.13) — potential player confusion, recommend differentiating. Margin art ('KayfaBINGO!', 'Stay fluffy!', 'ECG Punk', 'Chaos Corps', 'Chaos Theory Med') provides fertile ground for variant modes and future expansion naming.
